title: Termwise product cones remain limiting in the derived category
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products satisfying CountableAB4Star and a chosen derived category. For every countable type J and family C of integer-indexed cochain complexes in A, the image under DerivedCategory.Q of the termwise product limit cone of C is a limit cone. No products in the derived category are assumed.

proof.text: In the homotopy category, termwise products are products: maps and homotopies are componentwise. Exact countable products commute with homology and preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Represent a family of derived morphisms by left fractions L → M j ← C j; the product of denominators and the assembled numerator supply a lift.

For uniqueness write the difference as L → N ← P, with denominator s and P = ∏ C j. The left Ore condition and fraction equality criterion supply a j : N → M j and quasi-isomorphisms t j : C j → M j with s ≫ a j = π j ≫ t j and f ≫ a j = 0 in the homotopy category. Their product a satisfies s ≫ a = ∏ t j, so a is a quasi-isomorphism by two-out-of-three. Since all components of f ≫ a vanish, f ≫ a = 0; inverting a proves the difference zero. Transfer from Q(L) to an arbitrary vertex by essential surjectivity.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_termwiseProduct_isLimit
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [HasCountableProducts A] [CountableAB4Star A]
    (J : Type) [Countable J] (C : J → CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone (limit.cone (Discrete.functor C))))
